image_description: A top-down view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a surface. The organism displays an elongated oval shape with eight distinct, overlapping dorsal calcareous plates arranged in a linear series. These plates are embedded in a thick, textured, leathery girdle that forms the outer rim. The plates exhibit a mottled greenish-grey coloration with visible growth lines and texture. The head region is indistinct and blunt, lacking eyes or tentacles. No ventral foot is visible as the subject is viewed from the dorsal side.
